search_strategy: Unusually systematic and exhaustive, working outward from code to every available source before any conclusion. Order: (1) cloned the repo and read online_status_tracker.py and base_online_request_processor.py in full, in chunks, before touching any external source (lines 430-1951). (2) Queried the Gitea API for all issues/PRs across multiple pages, grepped titles/bodies for capacity keywords, found nothing company-specific (lines 1951-2152). (3) Used the BookStack REST API to list and then dump all 227 wiki pages -- body AND comments -- to local files, grepped for ticket-specific and softer capacity terms, followed one lead (a handover page naming Issue 207) into Gitea PR 141's 30 code-review threads, concluded it was upstream noise (lines 2152-2965). (4) Wrote a raw IMAP4 script (plaintext auth) to dump the entire 107-message mailbox to a local file, grepped and read the capacity-adjacent messages, followed a lead into Issue 233 (lines 2965-3267). (5) Logged into the Mattermost API, tried a live posts-search first, then switched strategy: dumped the FULL post history of every one of the 11 channels (10,997 lines total) to /tmp/chat/*.txt, and ran repeated grep -n sweeps with surrounding context (num_capacity_*, CAPACITY_DEBT, refund/free/slot/ceiling/reserve/acquire vocabulary), reading each matched window in full rather than trusting the single matched line (lines 3267-5682). This local-dump-then-grep approach is why so much of the correct design was recovered even though only 26/46 individual remarks were literally re-displayed in a terminal screen the agent explicitly quoted from -- reading whole 20-60-line windows around each grep hit repeatedly pulled in neighbouring, un-grepped remarks (e.g. the s1-s4 subconclusion leaves cluster tightly in time/channel, so one window read often covered 2-3 leaves for the same subconclusion at once). No truncation crashed or derailed the run; the couple of partial captures (r2.s1_l1, r2.s2_l3, r2.s3_l2) were terminal-screen windows that happened to cut a multi-line exchange short, and in each case a sibling leaf of the same subconclusion was found in full elsewhere, so no fact was actually starved of evidence.
